subject.title: Feature: Message continuation marker for batched input (cost savings)

question: Should OpenClaw support sender-controlled continuation markers, and if so should they be one signal within a shared inbound coalescing contract rather than a standalone queue mode?
rationale: The alternatives change public message latency, transcript construction, command handling, configuration shape, and interactions with existing timer-based debounce and active-run queues; source inspection cannot establish the intended product semantics.

options.title: Unified coalescing contract
options.body: Approve a generic opt-in pre-dispatch aggregation layer with explicit markers as one supported hold/flush signal alongside bounded timer behavior.

options.title: Marker-only mode
options.body: Add only explicit marker and timeout handling, accepting a separate batching policy beside existing debounce and queue behavior.

options.title: Keep timer-only behavior
options.body: Decline marker semantics and treat fixed or adaptive inbound debounce plus active-run collect/steer as the supported product answer.

recommendation.title: Unified coalescing contract
recommendation.body: Approve a generic opt-in pre-dispatch aggregation layer with explicit markers as one supported hold/flush signal alongside bounded timer behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history and discussion signals connect this person to shared inbound debounce, queue behavior, and the prior item-specific review.
